**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/03/03 (Fri) 02:06
- [FACT] The user has been trying to keep track of their expenses.
- [FACT] The user has been attending a lot of events lately.
- [PREFERENCE] The user is looking for a budgeting app that can categorize their spending.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended budgeting apps: 
  - **Mint**: Free, connects to bank accounts, tracks spending, categorizes expenses, offers bill tracking, credit score monitoring, and investment tracking (iOS and Android).
  - **Personal Capital**: Free, tracks income, expenses, investments, debts, and offers financial planning tools (iOS and Android).
  - **You Need a Budget (YNAB)**: Free trial, then $6.99/month or $83.99/year, assigns jobs to every dollar, offers automated savings, investment tracking, and bill tracking (iOS and Android).
  - **Spendee**: Free, user-friendly, tracks expenses by categorizing them, offers automated expense tracking, budgeting, and receipt scanning (iOS and Android).
  - **Wally**: Free, connects to bank accounts and credit cards, tracks expenses, categorizes them, offers bill tracking and investment tracking (iOS and Android).
  - **Pocketbook**: Free, tracks income and expenses, sets budgets, sends alerts when over budget, offers investment tracking and bill tracking (iOS and Android).
  - **Quicken**: Free trial, then $39.99/year, tracks spending, creates budgets, sets financial goals, offers investment tracking and bill tracking (iOS and Android).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested factors to consider when choosing a budgeting app: ease of use, features, connectivity, security, and cost.
